video_title: Crypto Is Shifting Gears + AI Router Wars - The Chopping Block
gist: The Chopping Block panel reads a macro-led crypto rebound - Bitcoin back over $80k on Treasury long-end buybacks and $2B of ETF inflows, Hyperliquid at an all-time high after Trump signaled CFTC work to onshore it - and argues the real US opening is agency rulemaking (the SEC's reg crypto $5M token-sale tier) rather than the stalled CLARITY Act. The longer half maps AI inference markets onto DeFi market structure: Stripe's $7B Open Router deal, cache-token price manipulation by inference providers, SaaS companies launching routers to earn payment-for-order-flow spreads, and Venice-style inference tokens as the next real token category.

insights.claim: Bitcoin has broken back above $80,000 (trading around $79,500 after tagging 80K), driven by a wave of short liquidations and over $2 billion of ETF inflows after a long stretch of quiet ETF demand.
insights.speaker: host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: Flow-driven squeeze plus returning ETF bid is the setup to watch: if inflows persist the move has follow-through, if they fade it was a liquidation-only rally.

insights.claim: Treasury Secretary Bessent buying back long-dated bonds and shifting issuance to the short end is being read as stimulative for risk assets and has revived the 'debasement trade' bid in gold and Bitcoin.
insights.speaker: host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: The crypto bid here is a macro/duration trade in disguise - watch long-end yields and Treasury buyback announcements as the leading indicator for the next leg in gold and BTC.
insights.quote: Secretary Bessant has started to try to pull in the long end of the curve buying back longdated bonds to issue short and all of that has been very stimulative of risk assets

insights.claim: Hyperliquid's HYPE token hit an all-time high above $80 after Trump said at a White House crypto summit that the CFTC chairman was working to bring Hyperliquid onshore in a compliant way.
insights.speaker: host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: Single-headline repricing of a DeFi asset on US access optionality - the token is now carrying regulatory-approval expectations that have zero implementation detail behind them.
insights.quote: working to bring Hyperlid into the United States in a fully compliant and legal fashion

themes.theme: Onshoring perps: the devil in the clearing details

insights.claim: Retail expectation that Americans will soon trade Hyperliquid freely from a Schwab-style account is wrong; the realistic outcome is a KYC-gated US deployment resembling what Lighter did with Robinhood in Europe, possibly with cross-deployment collateral interoperability.
insights.speaker: Tom (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: Prices a much narrower US TAM than the headline implies; fade positioning that assumes unrestricted US access to the offshore orderbook.
insights.quote: anyone in the US can just go use Hyperlid and it's going to be you know in in your Schwab account. I think that's like not going to happen.

insights.claim: Polymarket's structure is the blueprint for onshoring a DeFi venue: a separate KYC'd, surveilled US pool of liquidity that cannot trade against the permissionless offshore book, because regulators require the ability to unmask both sides of a trade.
insights.speaker: host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: Fragmented liquidity is the base case for any US-compliant perp DEX - model thinner US books and a persistent onshore/offshore basis rather than one global pool.

insights.claim: US regulators may refuse to approve auto-deleveraging (ADL) as a loss-absorption mechanism, forcing onshore perp venues toward conventional centralized clearing where a broker posts risk capital - making clearing and settlement, not KYC, the hardest part of the approval.
insights.speaker: Tarun (Gauntlet)
insights.so_what: A clearing-capital requirement would change the economics of onshore perp DEXs entirely and favors players who can partner with an existing FCM/clearing balance sheet.
insights.quote: how the the kind of clearing settlement stuff works because like that that's sort of where governments spend a lot of time writing law also

insights.claim: Legacy exchange incumbents will fight the onshoring of no-KYC decentralized venues because the absence of compliance friction is an overwhelming operational advantage, and the fight is already visible in CME's stock drop and Terry Duffy's public pushback on CNBC.
insights.speaker: Robert (Superstate)
insights.so_what: CME and other listed exchange incumbents are the natural short/underperform leg against a US perp-DEX approval narrative; expect lobbying-driven delay.
insights.quote: there's also going to be a lot of adversarial conflict with legacy incumbents as they watch something huge and new come in

insights.claim: More than half of Hyperliquid's volume is now in RWAs, which fall under a separate regulatory regime and further complicate standing up a compliant US version of the venue.
insights.speaker: host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: The RWA mix means an onshore Hyperliquid would need both CFTC and securities-side treatment - a materially slower path than a pure crypto perp approval.
insights.quote: more than half of their volume now is RWAS like obviously that exists under very different regulatory regime

insights.claim: The CLARITY Act is priced at roughly 15% on prediction markets to pass this year and about 50/50 by end-2028, so the SEC and CFTC are moving to deliver equivalent outcomes through rulemaking instead of legislation.
insights.speaker: host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: Agency rulemaking is reversible by a future administration in a way statute is not - regulatory-clarity trades built on CLARITY passing should be re-dated to 2027-2028.

insights.claim: The SEC's first crypto rulemaking, a 42-page 'regulation crypto assets' release with a 60-day comment window, creates a light-touch $5 million token-sale exemption, a $75 million-per-12-months tier requiring audited financials and ongoing reporting, and a conditional safe harbor letting a qualifying token exit securities treatment once managerial efforts lapse.
insights.speaker: host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: First real legal path to a US retail token crowdsale - watch which projects file, and the comment letters from crypto funds shaping the final rule.

insights.claim: The $75 million tier of the SEC's crypto fundraising rule will go essentially unused because its PCAOB-audit and reporting burden mirrors Reg A+ Tier 2, which almost nobody uses - if you are doing that much work you may as well file an S-1.
insights.speaker: Robert (Superstate)
insights.so_what: Ignore the headline $75 million number; the only economically live channel in the rule is the $5 million tier, at roughly $10-20k of legal cost versus hundreds of thousands for a PCAOB audit.
insights.quote: I don't think that many people are going to adopt it. Frankly, this is my contrary take. I don't think it's going to get used.

insights.claim: The rule is aimed at a 2017-era founder archetype that barely exists now: almost no team today pitches building a network and then walking away as it becomes self-sustaining, so the industry's real unresolved fight is asset categorization and how a centralized company's token accrues value, not fundraising mechanics.
insights.speaker: Tarun (Gauntlet)
insights.so_what: Regulatory relief on fundraising does not unlock the actual bottleneck for token valuations - keep watching for guidance on whether tokens can legally receive revenue from an operating company.
insights.quote: the crux of of you know the industry's beef with the SEC right now I think it's more around asset categorization what is a security what's not a security

insights.claim: Someone will arbitrage the $5 million cap by launching many tokens through a holding company with a dozen-plus subsidiary offerings, sharing the fixed legal cost so 15 raises cost roughly $100k rather than 15 times $20k.
insights.speaker: guest panelist (in Bhutan)
insights.so_what: Expect a token-factory business model to appear under the exemption, and expect the SEC to have to patch it - a live risk that the light-touch tier gets tightened.
insights.quote: someone who like memecoin style dodoses this legislation

insights.claim: Because LLMs collapse the fixed cost of navigating bureaucratic process, government services that were implicitly rationed by paperwork friction (refunds, ticket contests, comment letters) are being flooded - and the same removal of the administrative speed bump could overwhelm capital-markets gatekeepers like the SEC.
insights.speaker: host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: A reusable model for any regulated market: where compliance cost was the real quota, AI-driven cost collapse forces new hard limits - anticipate rule tightening wherever paperwork was the gate.
insights.quote: you have to kind of revisit what was effectively a speed bump that has now been removed from society

themes.theme: AI inference is rebuilding DeFi market structure

insights.claim: Stripe acquired Open Router, the LLM inference aggregator founded in 2023 by OpenSea co-founder Alex Atallah, for $7 billion - a price justified by explosive growth in inference demand and in open-weight models competing with the closed labs.
insights.speaker: host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: Routing/aggregation, not model training, just got a $7 billion comp - the layer that arbitrages between models is where a payments giant chose to buy.

insights.claim: The open-model inference stack maps one-for-one onto DeFi: the harness is the wallet/front end holding user secrets, the router is a DEX router, the model is the protocol, and inference providers are the liquidity providers or validators - and as in crypto, value accrues to the edges (harnesses and providers), not the middle.
insights.speaker: Tarun (Gauntlet)
insights.so_what: If value goes to the edges, own harness/app-layer or GPU-provider exposure rather than the routing middleware - and expect routers to be fee-compressed the way DEX aggregators were.
insights.quote: if you look at the lessons of crypto, it kind of tells you that the the value flows to the edges like it goes to the the liquidity providers or insurance providers or it goes to like the wallets

insights.claim: Months of scraped Open Router pricing data show inference providers manipulating headline prices in an MEV-like way - quoting cheap input/output tokens while under-reporting unverifiable cached tokens to raise the true all-in price - and many of the operators doing it come out of crypto or Ethereum mining.
insights.speaker: Tarun (Gauntlet)
insights.so_what: Advertised token prices are not comparable across providers; verification of caching claims is an unsolved, potentially fundable problem and a real cost leak for anyone routing at scale.
insights.quote: I'm going to give a lower price on the expensive tokens, like the input and output tokens, like the fresh ones, but uh but I'm actually just going to say I never use cash tokens, so I can kind of charge more.

themes.theme: Routers as the new toll booth on AI spend

insights.claim: SaaS incumbents that were being written off as AI roadkill are counterattacking by launching their own model routers - Ramp, Stripe, Databricks and Palantir all have one - monetizing their user data and query flow by taking a spread on tokens and routing part of the demand to cheap open/Chinese models instead of Anthropic.
insights.speaker: Tarun (Gauntlet)
insights.so_what: A concrete re-rating case for beaten-down SaaS names: routing is a new high-margin revenue line built on data they already own, and a structural leak in frontier-lab pricing power.
insights.quote: we're about to have the revenge of the SAS company like enterprise company because the last two years SAS company stocks have just been getting bludgeoned

insights.claim: Token routing is developing a payment-for-order-flow economy, with inference providers already cutting prices in exchange for guaranteed token volume, and Brett Harrison's extension that hedge funds will eventually pay for users' LLM query flow as a real-time read on the economy.
insights.speaker: host (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: Query flow is an emerging alternative dataset; whoever owns the harness or router controls a saleable, real-time economic signal before it shows up in prints.
insights.quote: the payment for order flow in token routing probably actually looks like hedge funds that will pay you for your LM queries just to get real-time information into what's happening in the economy

insights.claim: Open-weight model labs are defending against commoditization with BSL-style licenses - Kimi K3's new license is free for personal use but charges companies above roughly $20 million of revenue a fixed fee - a defense that depends entirely on the legal system and looks brittle.
insights.speaker: Tom (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: Licensing, not technology, is currently the only moat on open weights; if it fails to hold, model-layer margins go to zero and value shifts further to harnesses and inference.
insights.quote: it's very bslike where it's open weights you can use it for personal use but if you're a company with over you know 20 million revenue you have to pay us a licensing fee

themes.theme: Tokenized inference as the next token category

insights.claim: Venice-style inference tokens are the next token type with L1-scale potential: they deliver a digital good with revenue from day one, staking can be tied to quality of service such as discounted inference or zero data retention, and with the minimum AI equity raise now around $20 million there is room for a wave of smaller token-funded inference teams.
insights.speaker: guest panelist (in Bhutan)
insights.so_what: A cleanly valuable token category - unlike offchain RWAs, the good is digital and priceable; watch crypto teams pivoting into inference provision as the supply of these launches.
insights.quote: to me this is the next token type that will be the L1 potential

insights.claim: Providers already discount inference for users who waive zero data retention, which makes the 2017 'get paid for your data' token dream finally workable - AI now streams a user's data out in usable form, and labs are paying enormously for it, with Anthropic said to be spending $10 billion on data this year while inference itself runs at 90%+ margins.
insights.speaker: Tarun (Gauntlet)
insights.so_what: Data-for-rebates is a live business model and a reason to revisit 2017-era data tokens; also frames the cost side (data acquisition) versus margin side (inference) of the AI stack.
insights.quote: do you remember the 2017 token dream of like okay get paid for your data somehow use a token to do that whatever this is actually the first time I actually think that stuff will it might actually work

insights.claim: Non-crypto distributed-compute projects like dark bloom are rediscovering decentralized inference from first principles, and the resulting coordination layer will look like mining pools - but secured by statistical guarantees and a high cost of cheating rather than cryptographic proof.
insights.speaker: guest panelist (in Bhutan)
insights.so_what: Frames how value in distributed inference will be captured and where verification risk sits - the same trust gap that the caching-cheating data already exposes.
insights.quote: it's going to look like mining pools actually it's like it feels a lot more like mining pools except like you don't have cryptographic guarantees you have these like statistical guarantees

insights.claim: The current memecoin and social-trading mania is a US-specific phenomenon: Asian markets, stereotypically the degenerate ones, are notably less involved, and apps like FOMO have little awareness in Asia despite a large fundraise, prompting teams to try to localize the format.
insights.speaker: Tarun (Gauntlet)
insights.so_what: Untapped Asian demand for social-trading products is an expansion vector - and the one Chinese-character memecoin, Binance Life, is already rallying on page one of CoinMarketCap.
insights.quote: the US memecoin stuff is actually very crazy like like there's something weird about that that like it hasn't translated here

insights.claim: Most Asian teams are still building in the buttoned-up RWA and tokenization meta of the last two years - invoice factoring, FX, STO-style products - and were caught flat-footed by the sudden gear shift back to speculative markets, echoing the surprise when BlackRock's Larry Fink turned pro-Bitcoin ahead of the ETFs.
insights.speaker: Tom (Dragonfly)
insights.so_what: A positioning gap: builders are concentrated in RWA while flows rotate to speculation, which usually means an under-supplied set of products for the incoming retail cycle.
insights.quote: it feels like a lot of people were caught off guard with the shift
